steps.intent: China's primary objective is to preserve the 31 August ceasefire in Idlib while firmly defending Syrian sovereignty and ensuring that legitimate counter-terrorism operations against Security Council-designated terrorist groups (such as Hayat Tahrir al-Sham and ISIL) are not obstructed. The most contentious point of contention during negotiations will be the explicit counter-terrorism carve-out in operative paragraph 2, which Western members argue is used by Damascus and Moscow to legitimize indiscriminate military offensives and strikes on civilian areas. Additionally, Western delegations are likely to oppose language that conditions humanitarian access on strict respect for Syrian government sovereignty, preferring unconditional and cross-border mechanisms.

messages.Belgium: As humanitarian co-penholder, Belgium cannot accept a text that provides an open-ended counter-terrorism exemption to the cessation of hostilities, which in practice serves to legitimize military operations causing severe civilian casualties and the destruction of civilian infrastructure in Idlib. Counter-terrorism efforts can never excuse violations of international humanitarian law or the targeting of hospitals and schools. We urge the penholders instead to support the humanitarian co-penholders' draft resolution, which establishes a clear, unconditional cessation of hostilities to protect civilians and secure unhindered humanitarian access.
messages.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire remains deeply concerned by the humanitarian crisis in north-western Syria and underscores that counter-terrorism efforts must strictly adhere to international humanitarian law and avoid civilian harm. We strongly urge the co-sponsors to include explicit protections for civilian infrastructure, particularly hospitals and schools, in accordance with Council resolutions. Our delegation also encourages greater efforts to bridge divisions among Council members to achieve a unified and consensual approach to alleviating the suffering of the Syrian people.
messages.Dominican Republic: The Dominican Republic remains deeply concerned by the catastrophic humanitarian consequences of the ongoing military escalation in north-western Syria and the severe toll on innocent civilians. While we recognize the imperative of countering terrorism, counter-terrorist operations cannot serve as an open-ended justification to ignore international humanitarian law or continue attacks that devastate civilian infrastructure and medical facilities. We believe Council action must focus unconditionally on protecting civilians and securing an effective cessation of hostilities, in line with the humanitarian initiative led by Belgium, Germany, and Kuwait.
messages.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea commends the efforts of the penholders and fully supports the principles of Syrian sovereignty, territorial integrity, and the legitimate fight against Council-designated terrorist groups. However, to foster unity within the Council and ensure the effective protection of the civilian population in north-western Syria, the text should more explicitly balance counter-terrorism efforts with strict compliance with international humanitarian law and the protection of medical and humanitarian facilities. We encourage the co-sponsors to engage with all Council members to bridge differences and achieve a unified Council response.
messages.France: France cannot accept a draft that serves as a blank check for the Syrian regime and its allies to continue the relentless bombardment of civilian populations, hospitals, and schools under the guise of combating terrorism. Counter-terrorism efforts must comply strictly with international humanitarian law and cannot be exploited as a pretext for the slaughter of civilians in Idlib. Council action must genuinely focus on an immediate and unconditional cessation of hostilities and the full, unhindered delivery of cross-border humanitarian aid, as presented by the humanitarian co-penholders.
messages.Germany: As humanitarian co-penholder, Germany cannot accept a text that provides a carte blanche for the Syrian regime and its allies to continue devastating air strikes and shelling against civilians and civilian infrastructure under the pretext of counter-terrorism. Any genuine cessation of hostilities must prioritize the protection of more than three million civilians in north-western Syria and full respect for international humanitarian law. We urge the penholders to support the humanitarian draft presented by Belgium, Germany, and Kuwait instead of pursuing a parallel text that undermines the Council's humanitarian responsibilities.
messages.Indonesia: Indonesia attaches great importance to preserving Council unity and alleviating the dire humanitarian situation facing civilians in north-western Syria. While we fully recognize the legitimate fight against Council-designated terrorist groups, counter-terrorism operations must never be conducted at the expense of international humanitarian law and the protection of innocent civilians. We urge the co-sponsors to accommodate these elements to bridge divides within the Council and help build a viable consensus.
messages.Kuwait: As humanitarian co-penholder on Syria alongside Belgium and Germany, Kuwait cannot accept a text that provides broad exemptions legitimizing ongoing military operations that endanger over three million civilians in Idlib. The priority of the Security Council must be the unconditional protection of civilian lives, health-care facilities, and the safeguarding of humanitarian access in full compliance with international humanitarian law. We urge the penholders to support our humanitarian draft resolution, which faithfully reflects the urgent needs of the Syrian people and the calls of the United Nations humanitarian leadership.
messages.Peru: Peru believes that the protection of civilians and the catastrophic humanitarian situation in north-western Syria must remain the Council's paramount priority. Counter-terrorism operations cannot be used to justify indiscriminate attacks or bombings of civilian infrastructure, including hospitals and schools, nor to bypass international humanitarian law. Without clear guarantees on IHL compliance, accountability, and unimpeded humanitarian access, we cannot support this text.
messages.Poland: Poland cannot support a draft that provides a loophole for continued military offensives in north-western Syria under the guise of counter-terrorism. Measures against designated terrorist groups must strictly comply with international humanitarian law and cannot serve as a justification for the destruction of civilian infrastructure or the targeting of hospitals. We fully stand behind the humanitarian initiative put forward by Belgium, Germany, and Kuwait to achieve an immediate, unconditional cessation of hostilities in Idlib.
messages.Russian Federation: As a co-sponsor of this draft resolution, the Russian Federation fully supports the text as currently drafted. It correctly reflects the reality on the ground by welcoming the ceasefire announced on 31 August while unequivocally maintaining in operative paragraph 2 that the cessation of hostilities does not apply to Security Council-designated terrorist groups, including Hayat Tahrir al-Sham. We must maintain unity and resist any attempts to weaken the counter-terrorism carve-out or infringe upon the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic.
messages.South Africa: South Africa firmly believes that the primary objective of the Council must be to alleviate the suffering of civilians in north-western Syria through an effective cessation of hostilities and unhindered humanitarian access. While we acknowledge the legitimate need to combat Security Council-designated terrorist groups, all counter-terrorism operations must strictly comply with international humanitarian law and ensure the protection of civilians and critical infrastructure. We urge the penholders to work towards building consensus across the Council so that we can adopt a unified and constructive decision.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom cannot support a text that effectively provides a carte blanche for the Syrian regime and its allies to continue the relentless bombardment of civilians and civilian infrastructure in Idlib under the guise of counter-terrorism. The Council must rally behind the humanitarian resolution put forward by Belgium, Germany, and Kuwait, which genuinely prioritizes civilian protection and an immediate, unconditional cessation of hostilities. Any credible resolution must uphold international humanitarian law without loopholes and guarantee unimpeded cross-border humanitarian access.
messages.United States of America: The United States strongly opposes this draft, which serves only to provide political cover and a counter-terrorism loophole for the Syrian regime and the Russian Federation to continue their brutal military offensive against civilians in Idlib. We cannot accept text that legitimizes the ongoing bombardment of hospitals, schools, and internally displaced persons under the guise of fighting terrorism. The Council must instead rally behind the genuine humanitarian initiative drafted by Belgium, Germany, and Kuwait to secure an immediate and comprehensive cessation of hostilities.

Concurrently, the draft steadfastly preserves China's core principles by maintaining the vital counter-terrorism carve-out against Council-designated terrorist groups and reaffirming the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic.

messages.Belgium: Belgium, together with Germany and Kuwait as humanitarian co-penholders, cannot accept a text that maintains blanket counter-terrorism exemptions in OP2, which have repeatedly served as justification for indiscriminate offensives against civilians and civilian infrastructure in Idlib. Any resolution from this Council must establish an unconditional cessation of hostilities to protect over three million civilians and safeguard cross-border humanitarian delivery. Unless OP2 is completely removed, Belgium will vote against this draft.
messages.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire thanks the co-sponsors for accommodating our proposals regarding international humanitarian law and sustained humanitarian access. Nevertheless, my delegation deeply regrets the persistent divisions within the Council and the lack of convergence with the initiative led by the humanitarian co-penholders. In the absence of a unified approach and broad consensus to effectively alleviate the suffering of civilians in north-western Syria, Côte d’Ivoire cannot support the text and will abstain.
messages.Dominican Republic: The Dominican Republic appreciates the penholders' inclusion of references to international humanitarian law; however, we remain firmly opposed to retaining counter-terrorism exemptions in OP2 that can serve as a pretext for continued military operations against civilian areas in Idlib. Additionally, the draft must explicitly uphold vital cross-border humanitarian delivery mechanisms. Without these essential adjustments to protect civilians and secure humanitarian access, the Dominican Republic cannot support this draft.
messages.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea thanks the co-sponsors for constructively incorporating our proposals regarding the strict adherence to international humanitarian law in counter-terrorism operations and the protection of medical and educational facilities under resolution 2286 (2016). We believe the revised draft text strikes a necessary balance between addressing the grave humanitarian needs of civilians in north-western Syria and confronting the threat posed by Council-designated terrorist groups. We support the text as presented and encourage all Council members to seek common ground and unity.
messages.France: France cannot accept a draft that serves as a political justification for the ongoing military offensive by the Syrian regime and its allies in north-western Syria. The counter-terrorism carve-out in operative paragraph 2 effectively legitimizes strikes against civilian infrastructure and hospitals under the guise of combating terrorism. Without the deletion of this loophole and the explicit reaffirmation of the cross-border humanitarian mechanism established by resolution 2165 (2014), France will firmly oppose this text.
messages.Germany: Germany cannot accept a text that retains the counter-terrorism carve-out in operative paragraph 2, which fundamentally undermines the call for a genuine cessation of hostilities and gives green light to continued military offensives in Idlib. While we firmly oppose Council-designated terrorist groups, counter-terrorism measures must never override international humanitarian law or serve as a justification to bomb hospitals, schools, and civilian populations. As humanitarian co-penholder, Germany will vote against this text unless this fatal loophole is removed and cross-border access is fully safeguarded.
messages.Indonesia: Indonesia thanks China and the Russian Federation for their constructive engagement and for incorporating our proposals regarding international humanitarian law and the protection of humanitarian and medical personnel. However, Indonesia attaches the utmost importance to Council unity, particularly on humanitarian matters concerning the Syrian people. Given the profound divisions among Council members and the lack of consensus on this text, Indonesia cannot support the draft resolution and will abstain.
messages.Kuwait: As humanitarian co-penholder on Syria alongside Belgium and Germany, Kuwait cannot support a text that fails to provide a genuine, unconditional cessation of hostilities to protect the more than three million civilians trapped in Idlib. Retaining counter-terrorism carve-outs in operative paragraph 2 creates an unacceptable loophole that legitimizes ongoing military operations against populated areas and critical infrastructure. Furthermore, any resolution on the humanitarian situation must explicitly reaffirm the cross-border mechanism authorized under resolution 2449 (2018), which remains an irreplaceable lifeline for millions in need.
messages.Peru: Peru appreciates the penholders' inclusion of language on international humanitarian law in OP2 and OP5. However, we cannot support a text that maintains broad counter-terrorism exceptions that in practice undermine the cessation of hostilities and civilian protection in north-western Syria. Furthermore, the draft fails to address accountability for grave violations and omits essential references to cross-border humanitarian mechanisms under resolutions 2165 (2014) and 2449 (2018), which remain vital for millions of civilians in Idlib.
messages.Poland: Poland cannot support a draft that provides a loophole for continuing military operations against Idlib under the guise of counter-terrorism, while undermining humanitarian assistance to millions of civilians in need. Counter-terrorism measures must never serve as a pretext for violating international humanitarian law or bombing civilian infrastructure, including hospitals and schools. We urge the Council instead to unite behind an immediate, unconditional cessation of hostilities and unhindered cross-border humanitarian access.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation fully supports the draft resolution as co-sponsor. The current text strikes the necessary balance by recognizing the cessation of hostilities declared on 31 August, upholding the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic, and crucially preserving the clear exception for legitimate counter-terrorism operations against Security Council-designated terrorist groups like Hayat Tahrir al-Sham. We stand ready to vote in favour of this text as formulated.
messages.South Africa: South Africa appreciates the penholders' constructive approach in accommodating our proposals into OP2 and OP5, particularly regarding full compliance with international humanitarian law and the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure. However, South Africa remains deeply concerned by the sharp division within the Council on this critical humanitarian file, as competing drafts undermine the unified message needed to alleviate the suffering of the Syrian people. In the absence of consensus and broad agreement among Council members, South Africa cannot support this draft and will abstain.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom cannot support a draft resolution that retains a broad counter-terrorism exemption in OP2, which the Syrian regime and its allies routinely exploit as a pretext to bomb schools, hospitals, and civilian infrastructure in Idlib. Council action must deliver a genuine, comprehensive ceasefire that protects the civilian population, safeguards cross-border humanitarian delivery, and supports accountability, notably the Secretary-General's Board of Inquiry.
messages.United States of America: The United States cannot support a draft resolution that includes sweeping counter-terrorism carve-outs designed to provide diplomatic cover for the Syrian regime and Russia to continue their brutal military offensive and indiscriminate attacks against civilians in Idlib. This competing text deliberately seeks to divide the Council and undermine the genuine, balanced humanitarian initiative led by Belgium, Germany, and Kuwait. Unless the text demands an unconditional halt to the offensive and removes loopholes that justify atrocities under the guise of counter-terrorism, the United States will vote against it.

steps.summary: China, acting in close coordination with co-sponsor the Russian Federation, maintains the core architecture of the draft resolution. Upholding Syria's sovereignty, strictly adhering to General Assembly resolution 46/182, and preserving necessary exemptions for military operations against Security Council-designated terrorist organizations remain non-negotiable principles. Demands from Western members to delete counter-terrorism carve-outs and dilute Syrian sovereignty were therefore rejected.

reasons.Belgium: Belgium strongly opposes the draft resolution because it contains broad counter-terrorism exemptions that undermine the ceasefire in Idlib and fails to safeguard unhindered cross-border humanitarian access, directly rejecting our red lines.
reasons.China: As the primary sponsor of the draft resolution alongside the Russian Federation, China votes in favour to advance its balanced approach addressing both the humanitarian situation and the fight against Security Council-designated terrorist groups while defending Syrian sovereignty.
reasons.Côte d’Ivoire: In line with our position during negotiations and our consistent approach to non-consensual competing drafts on Syria, Côte d’Ivoire abstains while prioritizing Council unity and humanitarian relief.
reasons.Dominican Republic: The Dominican Republic votes against the draft resolution because our red line regarding the blanket counter-terrorism exemption in operative paragraph 2 was rejected, which risks being used to justify indiscriminate military operations affecting civilians in Idlib. This aligns with our position during negotiations and our consistent defense of international humanitarian law and the protection of civilians.
reasons.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea supports the draft resolution as it underscores the imperative of respecting Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity while appropriately addressing the counter-terrorism operations against designated terrorist groups in Idlib. As is our standard practice, we cast our vote in favour and reserve any remarks for after the voting procedure.
reasons.France: France opposes this rival draft resolution because it contains an unacceptable counter-terrorism loophole in operative paragraph 2 that the Syrian regime and its allies exploit to justify indiscriminate bombardments against civilians, hospitals, and schools in Idlib, while failing to uphold the essential cross-border humanitarian mechanism.
reasons.Germany: Germany opposes the draft resolution because its counter-terrorism exemption in operative paragraph 2 provides a pretext for ongoing military offensives against civilians in Idlib and ignores key humanitarian priorities championed by Germany and its co-penholders.
reasons.Indonesia: Indonesia maintains an independent, non-aligned foreign policy and consistently advocates for Council unity on the Syrian humanitarian track. Given the severe polarization among Council members and the lack of consensus on competing draft texts, Indonesia abstains on this draft resolution.
reasons.Kuwait: Kuwait co-penned the humanitarian resolution on Idlib alongside Belgium and Germany, and firmly opposes this alternative text because its counter-terrorism carve-outs provide a loophole that undermines a genuine ceasefire and endangers millions of civilians in north-western Syria.
reasons.Peru: Peru voted against the draft resolution because its essential red-line concerns regarding counter-terrorism carve-outs being used to undermine civilian protection and justify military operations in Idlib were rejected by the penholders. Furthermore, Peru stood aligned with the humanitarian co-penholders (Belgium, Germany, and Kuwait) in opposing a text that failed to adequately safeguard international humanitarian law and humanitarian access modalities.
reasons.Poland: Poland voted against the draft resolution because its essential red lines were rejected, notably the retention of broad counter-terrorism exemptions in OP2 that serve to legitimize indiscriminate attacks on civilians in Idlib, as well as the absence of explicit support for cross-border humanitarian mechanisms. Aligning with its EU and Western partners, Poland refuses to endorse a text that undermines international humanitarian law and protection of civilians.
reasons.Russian Federation: As a co-sponsor of this draft resolution alongside China, Russia fully supports the text, which preserves the crucial anti-terrorist exemption regarding operations in Idlib and upholds Syria's sovereignty.
reasons.South Africa: South Africa abstains on this draft resolution in line with its non-aligned stance, balancing the need to counter terrorism with grave concerns over the humanitarian impact of military operations in Idlib and Council divisions. Any explanation of vote will be delivered after the voting process has concluded.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom opposes the draft resolution because its counter-terrorism carve-out in operative paragraph 2 provides a loophole for the Syrian regime and Russia to justify indiscriminate attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure in Idlib, while our key amendments were rejected.
reasons.United States of America: The draft resolution includes a broad counter-terrorism exemption in operative paragraph 2 that provides political cover for the Syrian regime and the Russian Federation to continue unlawful strikes against civilians and civilian infrastructure in Idlib. As our red-line request to eliminate this loophole was rejected, the United States votes against the draft resolution.

before.China:
China, together with the Russian Federation, has submitted the draft resolution now before the Security Council. Our objective is clear: to genuinely improve the humanitarian situation on the ground in north-western Syria, to preserve the cessation of hostilities in Idlib, and to address the root causes of the suffering endured by the Syrian people.

The situation in Idlib cannot be divorced from the rampant presence of Security Council-designated terrorist organizations, in particular Hayat Tahrir al-Sham, which continue to attack civilians, use innocent people as human shields, and launch assaults against residential areas and government positions. Any ceasefire that fails to recognize the threat posed by terrorism and leaves terrorists free to operate will only perpetuate the conflict and destabilize the entire region. The draft resolution we have put forward explicitly emphasizes that the cessation of hostilities must be respected by all parties, while maintaining necessary counter-terrorism operations in strict accordance with international humanitarian law and the protection of civilians.

Furthermore, the draft resolution reaffirms the fundamental principles of the United Nations Charter, including full respect for the sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic. Humanitarian assistance must be guided by General Assembly resolution 46/182, free from politicization or double standards. We also welcome the important progress made toward the launch of the Constitutional Committee, which represents a vital step toward an inclusive, Syrian-led, and Syrian-owned political settlement in line with resolution 2254 (2015).

China calls on all Council members to take a constructive, objective, and responsible approach by voting in favour of this draft resolution, so as to truly help alleviate the humanitarian plight in Syria and promote lasting peace and stability.
before.Germany:
Germany will vote against the draft resolution submitted by China and the Russian Federation. 

As co-penholders of the humanitarian file on Syria alongside Belgium and Kuwait, our priority has always been the protection of the more than 3 million civilians trapped in Idlib. We cannot support a text that includes sweeping exemptions for counter-terrorism operations that are routinely used as a pretext to justify indiscriminate attacks, the destruction of civilian infrastructure, and the bombing of hospitals and schools. Counter-terrorism measures can never relieve parties of their obligations under international humanitarian law. Because our red-line concerns were disregarded, Germany will vote "no".
before.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation, together with the People's Republic of China, has presented this draft resolution in order to offer the Security Council a balanced, objective, and realistic text focused on addressing the genuine humanitarian and security challenges in north-western Syria. 

Unlike other initiatives that seek to create safe havens for internationally recognized terrorists and artificially shield Hayat Tahrir al-Sham and affiliated groups under the guise of humanitarian concern, our draft clearly and unequivocally reaffirms that the fight against terrorism cannot stop. The Security Council cannot tie the hands of sovereign States in combating terrorist groups designated by the Council itself. At the same time, our text emphasizes full compliance with international humanitarian law, the protection of civilians, and the urgent necessity of facilitating unhindered humanitarian assistance in respect of the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic.

Furthermore, our draft welcomes the announced cessation of hostilities while preserving the crucial exemption for operations against terrorists, and it supports the tangible political progress made toward convening the Constitutional Committee. We urge all members of the Council who genuinely care about the plight of the Syrian people and the eradication of terrorism to support our text.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
The United Kingdom will vote against this draft resolution. 

This text is a disingenuous attempt to distract from the draft resolution presented earlier by the humanitarian co-penholders—Belgium, Germany, and Kuwait—which Russia and China chose to veto. The draft resolution before us contains a wide-ranging counter-terrorism exemption in operative paragraph 2 that provides a carte blanche for the Syrian regime and its Russian allies to continue their devastating and indiscriminate military offensive in Idlib under the guise of fighting terrorism. 

Counter-terrorism operations cannot and must not be used as an excuse to bomb schools, hospitals, and civilian infrastructure, nor to displace hundreds of thousands of vulnerable people. Because this text fails to genuinely protect civilians or halt the violence in north-western Syria, the United Kingdom cannot support it.

after.Belgium:
Mr. President,

Belgium voted against the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation and China. 

Together with Germany and Kuwait, as humanitarian co-penholders on the Syrian file, our sole objective throughout these negotiations has been to alleviate the immense suffering of the more than 3 million civilians trapped in Idlib and north-western Syria. Earlier today, we deeply regretted the vetoes cast by two permanent members against our draft resolution, which aimed to establish an immediate cessation of hostilities and protect innocent lives.

We could not support the text that was just put to the vote. Operative paragraph 2 includes a broad counter-terrorism exemption that fundamentally undermines the call for a cessation of hostilities. While Belgium is fully committed to the fight against terrorism and recognizes the threat posed by Council-designated terrorist groups such as Hayat Tahrir al-Sham, the fight against terrorism can never justify indiscriminate attacks against civilians, the bombing of hospitals and schools, or the collective punishment of an entire population. 

Counter-terrorism operations must strictly abide by international humanitarian law, including the core principles of distinction, precaution, and proportionality. The text proposed today creates an unacceptable loophole that provides cover for continued military offensives and the ongoing destruction of civilian infrastructure under the pretext of combating terrorism.

Belgium will remain steadfast in its commitment to the Syrian people, to the upholding of international humanitarian law, and to finding a lasting political solution in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015).

I thank you.
after.Côte d’Ivoire:
Mr. President,

My delegation wishes to explain its vote on the draft resolutions that have just been considered by the Security Council.

Côte d’Ivoire deeply regrets that, once again, divisions within the Council have prevented us from speaking with one voice on the tragedy facing the Syrian people, particularly in north-western Syria. 

My delegation abstained in the voting on the draft resolution contained in document S/2019/757, submitted by China and the Russian Federation. While Côte d’Ivoire reaffirms its resolute commitment to the fight against terrorism in all its forms and manifestations, we maintain that counter-terrorism operations must be conducted in strict compliance with international law, in particular international humanitarian law and international human rights law. The fight against terrorist groups designated by the Security Council cannot justify attacks on civilians, civilian infrastructure, schools, and medical facilities, nor can it impede rapid, safe, and unhindered humanitarian access to populations in distress.

Côte d’Ivoire remains deeply concerned by the alarming humanitarian situation in Idlib and the continued suffering of millions of innocent civilians caught in the crossfire. We reiterate that there can be no military solution to the Syrian conflict. Lasting peace can be achieved only through an inclusive, Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process under the auspices of the United Nations, in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015) and the 2012 Geneva Communiqué. In that regard, we welcome the progress made toward the establishment of the Constitutional Committee and encourage all Syrian parties to engage constructively in this process.

Finally, Côte d’Ivoire urges all members of the Security Council to overcome their differences and unite around the primary objective of protecting civilian lives and alleviating the immense suffering of the Syrian people.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.France:
(spoke in French):

France voted against the draft resolution presented by the Russian Federation and China. We deeply deplore the double veto cast earlier by those two permanent members against the draft resolution submitted by the humanitarian co-penholders—Belgium, Germany and Kuwait—which was supported by 12 members of the Security Council.

The text submitted by Russia and China was an obvious diversionary manoeuvre that does not address the humanitarian tragedy unfolding in north-western Syria. 

France voted against this draft resolution because it contains sweeping counter-terrorism exemptions that are unacceptable. While the fight against terrorism is an absolute priority for France, as it is for the international community, it cannot and must not be used as a pretext or an alibi to justify the indiscriminate bombing of civilians, the systematic destruction of hospitals, schools and humanitarian infrastructure, and the massive displacement of hundreds of thousands of people. Counter-terrorism operations can never relieve parties to the conflict of their strict obligations under international humanitarian law, in particular the principles of distinction, precaution and proportionality. The text put forward today provided a blank check to the Syrian regime and its allies to continue their brutal military offensive in Idlib under the guise of fighting terrorism.

More than 3 million civilians are trapped in Idlib, including over 1 million children. What is urgently needed is an immediate, verifiable and unconditional cessation of hostilities, the full respect of international humanitarian law, and safe, unhindered and sustained humanitarian access to all populations in need.

Finally, France reiterates that there is no military solution to the Syrian crisis. Only an inclusive, credible political process led under United Nations auspices, in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015), can bring lasting peace to Syria and stability to the region.
after.Indonesia:
Indonesia is deeply concerned by the deteriorating humanitarian situation in north-western Syria, particularly in Idlib, where millions of innocent civilians continue to suffer the devastating consequences of escalating violence.

Indonesia has consistently maintained that the Council must put the humanitarian interests of the Syrian people above political differences. It is deeply regrettable that, once again, the Security Council has been unable to unite and speak with one voice when the lives of millions of civilians are at stake.

My delegation voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted earlier by the humanitarian co-penholders (S/2019/756), because our foremost priority is to halt the violence, protect civilians and civilian infrastructure, and ensure rapid, safe, and unhindered humanitarian access to all those in need. 

With regard to the draft resolution just voted upon (S/2019/757), Indonesia decided to abstain. While we recognize that the presence of Security Council-designated terrorist groups in north-western Syria poses a real and serious threat, we firmly believe that counter-terrorism operations must strictly comply with obligations under international law, particularly international humanitarian law and human rights law. The fight against terrorism can never justify the collateral damage inflicted on innocent civilians or the destruction of essential civilian infrastructure, including schools and medical facilities.

Indonesia reiterates its full commitment to the sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic. There can be no military solution to the conflict. A sustainable end to the suffering of the Syrian people can be achieved only through an inclusive, Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process facilitated by the United Nations, in line with resolution 2254 (2015).

In conclusion, Indonesia once again calls upon all members of the Security Council to set aside divisions and work collectively toward a unified position that genuinely serves the interests and alleviates the suffering of the Syrian people.
after.Kuwait:
(spoke in Arabic): At the outset, the State of Kuwait expresses its deep regret at the failure of the Security Council to adopt the draft resolution submitted by the humanitarian co-penholders—Belgium, Germany and Kuwait—owing to the use of the veto, despite having received the support of 12 members of the Council.

Our draft resolution was purely humanitarian in nature. Its sole aim was to alleviate the tragic suffering of more than 3 million civilians trapped in Idlib and north-western Syria, to put an end to the bloodshed, to protect innocent lives and civilian infrastructure, including schools and hospitals, and to ensure safe, unimpeded and sustainable humanitarian access to all those in need, in full accordance with international humanitarian law. Over the course of weeks of intensive, transparent and constructive negotiations, the co-penholders made every possible effort to accommodate the concerns of Council members and to preserve Council unity. It is therefore deeply disappointing that the Council was once again prevented from fulfilling its primary responsibility under the Charter of the United Nations.

With regard to the draft resolution submitted by China and the Russian Federation, the State of Kuwait voted against it. While we fully reaffirm our firm condemnation of terrorism in all its forms and manifestations and reiterate the necessity of combating terrorist groups designated by the Security Council, counter-terrorism operations must never be conducted at the expense of civilian lives or serve as a pretext to circumvent obligations under international humanitarian law, particularly the principles of distinction, precaution and proportionality. The draft resolution put forward did not adequately address these essential humanitarian concerns and failed to provide meaningful protection to civilians on the ground.

In conclusion, we reaffirm that there can be no military solution to the crisis in Syria. The only path forward is an inclusive, Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process facilitated by the United Nations, in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015) and the Geneva Communiqué of 2012. The State of Kuwait, together with the other co-penholders, will continue its steadfast efforts to address the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Syria and to stand by the brotherly Syrian people.
after.South Africa:
Mr. President,

South Africa expresses its deep regret that, once again, the Security Council has demonstrated division and has been unable to find common ground on the critical and deteriorating humanitarian situation in the Syrian Arab Republic, particularly in north-western Syria. 

South Africa abstained on the draft resolution submitted by China and the Russian Federation. While South Africa recognizes the legitimate threat posed by Security Council-designated terrorist groups and acknowledges the sovereign right of States to fight terrorism, we maintain that any counter-terrorism operations must strictly adhere to international law, in particular international humanitarian law, international human rights law, and refugee law. Military operations must always respect the principles of distinction, precaution, and proportionality, and must ensure the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, including medical and educational facilities. 

Counter-terrorism measures cannot be used to justify indiscriminate violence or the collective suffering of innocent civilians trapped in conflict zones. At the same time, we reiterate that humanitarian concerns should never be politicized or used to shield designated terrorist organizations.

South Africa firmly believes that there can be no military solution to the conflict in Syria. The only path to lasting peace is an inclusive, Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process that reflects the legitimate aspirations of all Syrian people, in full accordance with resolution 2254 (2015) and the Geneva Communiqué. In this regard, we welcome the progress made toward the convening of the Constitutional Committee and urge all parties to engage constructively under the auspices of the United Nations.

We urge all Council members to bridge their differences and work constructively together in unity to alleviate the immense suffering of the Syrian people and to support a comprehensive and peaceful political settlement that preserves the sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity of Syria.

I thank you.
after.United States of America:
The United States voted "no" on this draft resolution, and the overwhelming majority of Council members rejected it, because it is nothing more than a cynical attempt by Russia and China to distract from their unconscionable vetoes of the humanitarian resolution drafted by Belgium, Germany, and Kuwait earlier today.

The co-penholders put forward a balanced, principled text aimed solely at halting the bloodshed in Idlib, protecting more than 3 million innocent civilians, and upholding international humanitarian law. Russia and China chose instead to veto that effort, protecting the Assad regime at the expense of millions of Syrian men, women, and children.

The draft resolution put forward by Russia and China was not a serious humanitarian initiative. It was designed to provide diplomatic cover and a green light for the Assad regime and its Russian allies to continue their brutal military offensive in north-western Syria under the false pretense of counter-terrorism. 

Let us be completely clear: the United States is resolute in our commitment to defeating terrorism, including Al-Qaida and ISIS. But counter-terrorism operations can never excuse or justify the deliberate and indiscriminate bombing of hospitals, schools, markets, and civilian homes. Fighting terrorism does not relieve any party of its fundamental obligations under international humanitarian law.

By decisively rejecting this draft resolution today, the Security Council has sent an unmistakable message: we will not endorse or legitimize atrocities masquerading as counter-terrorism. The United States will continue to stand firmly with the Syrian people and support a genuine cessation of hostilities and a political solution in line with resolution 2254 (2015).
